partners.mechanism_chain: Carboxypeptidase N (CPN1) (HGNC:2423) —DISRUPTS→ Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-190892); Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-190892) —LEADS_TO→ Angioedema (HP:0002342); Complement Component 1 Q Subunit B (C1QB) (HGNC:2094) —BINDS→ Complement Component 1 Q (C1q) complex (GO:0005577); Complement Component 1 Q (C1q) complex (GO:0005577) —DISRUPTS→ Complement System Activation (GO:0006955); Complement System Activation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:00114210); Complement Component 1 Q (C1q) complex (GO:0005577) —DECREASES→ Kinin-Kallikrein System (REACT:R-HSA-190892). Loss-of-function mutations in CPN1 lead to impaired degradation of kinin-kallikrein system peptides, potentially causing angioedema. Loss-of-function mutations in C1QB impair the formation and function of the C1q complex, a key initiator of the classical complement pathway. The C1q complex also plays a role in clearing immune complexes and cellular debris, and its deficiency can lead to dysregulation of immune responses and increased susceptibility to infections. Furthermore, impaired C1q function can indirectly affect the kinin-kallikrein system by altering inflammatory processes and immune complex handling, potentially exacerbating conditions like angioedema or contributing to other immune-related phenotypes.
